title: Latitudinal diversity gradient
sub: Symposium topic 5 (your group) · Willig et al. 2003 vs Brodie & Mannion 2023
blurb: Why biodiversity peaks in the tropics, the three dimensions of diversity, and the exceptions.
h1: Latitudinal gradients in biodiversity: how and why?
lede: Your group's topic. Why does biodiversity peak in the tropics and fall toward the poles, and does that hold for every dimension? Classic: Willig, Kaufman & Stevens (2003). Recent: Brodie & Mannion (2023), the hierarchy of factors predicting the LDG.
six: **Latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG)**: species richness rises from the poles to the equator, across most groups.
Three dimensions: **taxonomic** (counting species), **functional** (counting jobs), **phylogenetic** (measuring shared history).
Spatial scales: point, **alpha** (one community), **beta** (difference between communities), **gamma** (many communities).
Causes in order of priority: **climate & energy** (main driver), habitat area, evolutionary history, biotic factors.
Diversification = speciation minus extinction. Tropical conservatism: most lineages evolved in, and stayed adapted to, tropical conditions.
Exceptions: parasites, aquatic plants (peak in temperate zones), secondary marine mammals and birds (higher toward poles).
foot: Source: Group 5 symposium slides; glossary section 6 a–e.

questions.q: What is the latitudinal diversity gradient?
questions.answer: Species richness rises from the poles to the equator
wrong: Species richness rises toward the poles
Body size increases toward the poles
Diversity is equal at all latitudes
questions.e: A global, general pattern across most groups.

questions.q: According to Group 5 (after Brodie & Mannion), what is the main driver of the LDG?
questions.e: Order: climate & energy → habitat area → evolutionary history → biotic factors.

questions.q: Which order of priority did Group 5 give for LDG causes?
questions.answer: Climate & energy, habitat area, evolutionary history, biotic factors
wrong: Biotic factors, habitat area, climate, history
Evolutionary history, climate, biotic factors, area
Habitat area, biotic factors, history, climate
questions.e: Brodie & Mannion 2023: a hierarchy of factors.

questions.answer: The range of traits and ecological roles in a community
wrong: The total branch length of a phylogeny
questions.e: 'Counting jobs': diet, body size, dispersal mode.

questions.answer: How much evolutionary history a community contains
questions.e: Usually as total branch length or relatedness.

questions.answer: How many species there are and how evenly individuals are spread among them
The difference in species between communities
wrong: Diversity at a single sample point
questions.e: Point → alpha (one community) → beta (difference) → gamma (many communities).

questions.answer: Most lineages evolved under tropical conditions and stayed adapted to them
wrong: Tropical species are protected by law
Temperate species move to the tropics
The tropics have the fewest species
questions.e: Part of the historical explanation of the LDG.

questions.q: When are latitudinal gradients sharper, according to Group 5?
questions.answer: In cold periods of Earth's history
questions.e: In hot climates the tropical zone is bigger.

questions.q: Which group was an exception, with diversity peaking in temperate zones?
questions.e: Exceptions: parasites, aquatic flora, secondary marine mammals and birds.

questions.answer: Reverse the gradient, with higher diversity in polar and temperate zones
wrong: Follow the classic gradient most strongly

questions.q: Which is one of the methodological problems in studying the LDG?
wrong: There is no data from the tropics
Species cannot be counted at all
questions.e: Problems: defining area, sampling effort, evolutionary rates.

questions.q: Which is an application of understanding the LDG named by Group 5?
questions.e: Also predicting invasive spread and future biodiversity.
